slot.brief: Order given alkyl halides by SN2 reactivity / leaving group ability and identify correct sequence.

stem: The correct decreasing order of reactivity of alkyl halides towards an $\text{S}_\text{N}2$ reaction for a given alkyl group $R$ is:

verdicts.working: SN2 rate depends on leaving-group ability, which follows C–X bond strength: C–I (213) < C–Br (285) < C–Cl (327) < C–F (485 kJ/mol). Weakest bond / best leaving group reacts fastest, so RI > RBr > RCl > RF.

working:
In an $	ext{S}_	ext{N}2$ reaction, the rate depends critically on the ability of the halide ion to depart (leaving group ability) as well as the carbon–halogen ($	ext{C}-	ext{X}$) bond strength.

1. Leaving group ability is inversely related to basicity. Since the conjugate acid strength is $	ext{HI} > 	ext{HBr} > 	ext{HCl} > 	ext{HF}$, the halide basicity order is $	ext{I}^- < 	ext{Br}^- < 	ext{Cl}^- < 	ext{F}^-$. The weaker the base, the better it serves as a leaving group. Hence, leaving group ability follows $	ext{I}^- > 	ext{Br}^- > 	ext{Cl}^- > 	ext{F}^-$.

2. The $	ext{C}-	ext{X}$ bond dissociation enthalpy decreases in the order: $	ext{C}-	ext{F} > 	ext{C}-	ext{Cl} > 	ext{C}-	ext{Br} > 	ext{C}-	ext{I}$. Thus, the $	ext{C}-	ext{I}$ bond is the weakest and easiest to break.

Both factors make the reactivity order for a given alkyl group:
$$R	ext{I} > R	ext{Br} > R	ext{Cl} > R	ext{F}$$

Option A reverses the sequence by mistakenly assuming reactivity follows electronegativity or bond polarity of the C-X bond.
Option C incorrectly ranks bromide higher than iodide.
Option D incorrectly transposes chloride and bromide, violating the periodic trend in leaving group ability.
